case_name: Prabhakar Shankar Dhuri v Sh. S. G. Pradhan and Others
facts: The petitioner, Prabhakar Shankar Dhuri, was detained by order of the Commissioner of Police on April 24, 1970.
He prepared a representation to be submitted to the Government of Maharashtra on May 1, 1970, and it was received on May 9, 1970.
The Government was required to refer the case to the Advisory Board within 30 days of detention, but this did not happen until after the representation was made.
A communication rejecting the representation was sent on June 9, 1970, more than 12 days after the date on which the Government was required to refer the case to the Advisory Board.
issues: Whether the Maharashtra Preventive Detention Act No. 18 of 1970 infringes the guarantee of the fundamental freedom under Articles 19, 21 and 22 of the Constitution.
The nature of the jurisdiction exercised by the Advisory Board and by the State Government in dealing with the representation made by the detenu detained under the Act.
petitioner_arguments: The petitioner is entitled to be released due to certain facts disclosed by the record.
court_reasoning: A delay of 16 days in disposing of a representation submitted by a detenu of the Government is a long delay where a person is detained without a trial under a special law relating to Preventive Detention.
The State of Maharashtra sent an intimation rejecting the representation one month 12 days after the petitioner was taken in custody, and 27 days after the representation was received.
holding: Following the judgment in Durga Show's case (supra) referred to above we direct that the detenu be released forthwith.
